intentions.title: Give every JS SDK capability a copy-pasteable, runnable canonical example instead of prose-only docs
intentions.evidence: 8 numbered snippets (01-08) each carry an 'Expected:' comment block documenting exact runtime output/status codes, covering create/publish, filtered query, SSE listen, optimistic mutate, publish/unpublish, server-component fetch, server-action mutate, and webhook revalidate — a runnable spec-by-example for the whole @barkpark/core + @barkpark/nextjs surface.

intentions.title: Prove the transaction → publish lifecycle (draft create, commit, explicit publish/unpublish) as the sanctioned mutation pattern
intentions.evidence: 01-create-document.ts uses client.transaction().create().commit() then a separate client.publish(); 05-publish-unpublish.ts round-trips actions.publish/unpublish and asserts _draft flips true/false — establishing draft-then-publish as the required two-step, never a direct write-to-published.

intentions.title: Make the DocsBuilder query API (where/order/limit/offset/findOne) the discoverable, typed way to filter content
intentions.evidence: 02-query-with-filters.ts chains client.docs<Post>('post').where(...).order(...).limit(5).find() and a separate findOne(), typed via BarkparkDocument generics.

intentions.title: Deliver real-time content updates to consumers via a typed SSE stream with clean subscribe/unsubscribe semantics
intentions.evidence: 03-listen-for-updates.ts uses client.listen<Post>() as an async iterator, handles a 'welcome' event with eventId, and unsubscribes via handle.unsubscribe() on a timer/finally block.

intentions.title: Ship first-class Next.js integration (Server Components, Server Actions, optimistic client mutation, webhook-driven ISR) so Barkpark is a drop-in headless CMS for App Router apps
intentions.evidence: 06-server-component-fetch.tsx (createBarkparkServer + barkparkFetch with next.tags), 07-server-action-mutate.tsx ('use server' + defineActions createDoc/patchDoc), 04-mutate-optimistic.tsx (useOptimisticDocument with conflict banner), 08-revalidate-on-webhook.ts (createWebhookHandler + revalidateBarkpark) together cover the full read/write/realtime Next.js surface.

intentions.title: Enforce tag-scoped cache invalidation so a single document mutation only revalidates the Next.js cache entries it actually affects
intentions.evidence: 06-server-component-fetch.tsx wires next.tags = ['bp:ds:<dataset>:_all', 'bp:ds:<dataset>:type:<type>']; 07-server-action-mutate.tsx expects revalidateTag() fan-out to ['bp:ds:production:doc:<id>', 'bp:ds:production:type:post']; 08-revalidate-on-webhook.ts narrows webhook payloads into doc:<id>+type:<type> tags via revalidateBarkpark().

intentions.title: Make webhook-triggered revalidation secure and idempotent under retries and secret rotation
intentions.evidence: 08-revalidate-on-webhook.ts requires HMAC verification (401 bad_signature/stale), deduplicates retried deliveries via an LRU window (200 {deduped:true}), rejects non-POST (405), and supports a previousSecret for zero-downtime secret rotation.
